newsitem.title: UK: Agreement within reach at Amsterdam - UK's Cook.
newsitem.headline: Agreement within reach at Amsterdam - UK's Cook.

text.p: A deal over the stability pact designed to underpin the European Union's single currency is within reach at the EU summit in Amsterdam, British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Monday.
"The bones of an agreement are in place," Cook told BBC radio from Amsterdam.

Cook said the agreement, aimed at resolving a Franco-German dispute over whether the managers of the single currency should put jobs before monetary austerity, would entail a declaration on the importance of growth and jobs as policy objectives.
But he said that would not be done in a way that fudged the convergence criteria that will determine which countries qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU).

"We believe that that's the right strategy because if there is going to be a single currency it has to be based on credible criteria and on a credible basis -- but that needs to be within the overall context of putting jobs first," Cook said.
Cook restated the new Labour government's view that Britain is unlikely to join EMU in the first wave.
Quizzed about possible delays to EMU, Cook said it would be wrong for Britain to thwart countries that were determined to press ahead.
"But we do strongly take the view that it is more important that the single currency is credible when it goes ahead than the date on which it goes ahead.
"And if they do have to make a choice, I think the area where there should be any room for change would be the timteable rather than its credibility," he said.
